name: Automated 4.4 K wafer-scale probing of superconductor IC process-control monitors (Josephson junctions, SQUIDs, inductors, vias) on 200-mm wafers
plain_name: Automatically probe thousands of superconducting test circuits across a 200 mm wafer at 4 K
description: Load 200-mm SFQ5ee wafers through a vacuum load-lock onto a liquid-helium-cooled chuck, step a 20-pin DC probe card across 49 process-control-monitor groups inside mu-metal shielding with field-cancelling coils, and measure junction resistance, energy gap, inductance and via critical currents at 4.4 K.
keywords: Automatically probe thousands of superconducting test circuits across a 200 mm wafer at 4 K

sources.citation: Wafer-Scale Characterization of a Superconductor Integrated Circuit Fabrication Process, Using a Cryogenic Wafer Prober (West, Kurlej, Wynn, Rogers, Gouker, Tolpygo, arXiv:2112.00705; IEEE Trans. Appl. Supercond. 2022)

reported_equipment: fully automated cryogenic wafer prober developed at HPD/FormFactor, Inc.
DC probe card with 20 flexible tungsten probes

requirements.rationale: All process-control monitors were measured at 4.4 K.
The DC probe card has 20 tungsten probes, each needing a DC line.
Test structures are contacted through probe pins on the contact pads.
Wafers are transferred and probed in vacuum on the cryogenic chuck.
Optional: the chamber and handler were at better than 1e-6 Torr.
Optional: a mu-metal shield inside the 4 K radiation shield limits flux trapping in the SQUIDs and junctions.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
